| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | *(pending)* |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** eWiC is not a standalone journal but an open-access BCS conference-proceedings series ('the broadest possible range of topics ... subject only to the workshops being firmly established in the computing sciences'). It publishes the proceedings of many independently organized, recurring computing workshops/conferences (e.g. EVA London - Electronic Visualisation and the Arts, running annually since 2008; HCI conference volumes). Volumes require conformance to eWiC's 'key quality criteria for conference publication' and mandatory publication templates (PDF/Word/LaTeX).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Conference/workshop papers across the breadth of computing sciences (topic depends entirely on which hosted conference is targeted), Electronic visualisation and digital arts research (via EVA London), Human-Computer Interaction research (via BCS HCI conference volumes)

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- https://eva-london.org/publications/
- https://ewic.bcs.org/category/19269
- https://www.bcs.org/about-us/learned-publishing/electronic-workshops-in-computing-ewic/
- https://www.bcs.org/media/9409/publishing-policy.pdf
- https://www.scienceopen.com/hosted-document?doi=10.14236%2Fewic%2FEVA2025.0

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **ai_policy.leniency_1_5 / gate**: No eWiC-specific or BCS-wide generative-AI authorship/use policy was found on the eWiC page or in the BCS 2021 Publishing Policy PDF; individual hosted conferences may set their own but none was systematically checked.
- **preprint.allowed**: No preprint policy statement found on the eWiC page, the BCS Publishing Policy PDF, or hosted-conference publication pages surveyed.
- **experiential.review_time_months**: SciRev has no listing/reviews for eWiC (it is a proceedings series, not a submission-tracked journal); no forum discussion found on Reddit r/AskAcademia.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No first-hand data source found; eWiC does not centrally track this (review happens per hosted conference).
- **experiential.acceptance_note**: No first-hand author accounts found in English or Chinese-language academic forums.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: Zero hits on 小木虫/muchong.com, 知乎/zhihu, and Reddit r/AskAcademia for 'Electronic Workshops in Computing' or 'eWiC' — no concrete source to anchor a subjective claim, per hard rule against inventing reviewer-culture narrative.
- **peer_review.type (precise)**: eWiC itself does not publish a single peer-review standard; it is confirmed only that review is delegated to each hosted conference's program committee (one example found: BCS Interaction Group states its program committee carries out 'full peer review'), but no eWiC-wide blind/open type statement exists.

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
- 小木虫 muchong.com — searched "Electronic Workshops in Computing" — 0 relevant results (only generic forum/journal-review-list pages unrelated to eWiC)
- 知乎 zhihu.com — searched "Electronic Workshops in Computing" 知乎 — 0 relevant results (only generic 小木虫 topic pages, unrelated)
- Reddit r/AskAcademia — searched "eWiC" BCS reddit AskAcademia — 0 relevant results
- SciRev — no dedicated review page found for eWiC (searched via general web search; series is proceedings-based so unlikely to be tracked)
